task_name: Guard, parity assertions, counter repair and write trigger

concerns_addressed: Cycle 1 no data RED: accepted; T7 migrated_to_id scoping already made re-run a no-op; guard IF NOT EXISTS (un-migrated) RETURN sits before pre-check, temp tables and assertions, so no assertion can run when nothing is un-migrated.
Cycles 2, 5, 6, 7 regression guards: accepted with mutation proof; parity mutation cases were genuinely RED.
Gate: guard.sql counter repair and trigger sit behind work_item_merge.enabled = 'on'; parity assertions are inside the gated copy block. Gate-off path pinned by cycle 7.
Assertions scoped to wim_pending (rows with migrated_to_id IS NULL at start of this run); no whole-table comparisons; all messages start with 'work-item-merge:' and name workspace and key.
Trigger is BEFORE INSERT only, created only if absent AND a migrated row exists, creation conditional, trigger dropped with the table. No UPDATE/SELECT blocking.

Normal-restart crash-loop check: no RAISE EXCEPTION can fire when no un-migrated rows exist (early RETURN). schema.sql/agent/chat SQL only UPDATE tracker_items (line 931), never INSERT, so the trigger cannot trip a restart.
Dockerfile COPY: dist is built by tsc (no .sql emitted); COPY target ./server/dist/db/ matches migrate.js here; wiring assertion added to expand test.
Out-of-scope edits (Dockerfile, test-support extraction, T7 notice filter): justified; event-write routing check passes.
git diff --stat shows 8 files, none of the user's .gitignore or deploy/*school* files.

Risk (a): schema.sql 816-869 key backfill runs before the merge in the same transaction, only touches cards with NULL keys, and already raises counters past tracker and card MAX; on re-run it is a no-op, so it does not conflict with the repair. The T8 repair is monotonic (counter < max only) and mostly redundant defense in depth.
Risk (b): counter MAX is over cards with key_number NOT NULL, soft-deleted included (no deleted_at filter); covered by test.

Risk (c): trigger function work_item_merge_block_tracker_insert survives DROP TABLE; documented in guard.sql with the cleanup statement for the schema-removal task. Not carried to a later task file by this diff.
Risk (d): copy pre-check is scoped to ti.migrated_to_id IS NULL, so already migrated rows and their cards never self-collide.

Cycle 2: parity block moved to guard.sql runs after work-item-merge.sql in the same applySchema transaction (migrate.ts lines 39-40). Copy block creates wim_pending/wim_focus only after both early RETURNs (gate off, no un-migrated rows), so on a re-run or gate-off the tables do not exist and to_regclass IS NULL returns before any assertion; no empty-snapshot case, no false RAISE. When the copy ran, the new block sees the same ON COMMIT DROP snapshot and the same messages; assertion SQL moved verbatim. No new RAISE on normal restart.

strengths: Run-once early return makes post-go-live restarts a true no-op; assertions cannot see user edits
Assertions report first offending workspace/key/field via ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 with readable messages
Guard file is gated, idempotent, INSERT-only trigger with pg_trigger existence check
Atomicity proven from a second connection on the same scratch search_path with a positive control
Mutation proof for every regression-guard cycle; gate-off path pinned
Lint, event-write routing and tsc-visible changes clean in the audited range

Parity assertions now live in guard.sql with a double gate (enabled flag and to_regclass on both temp tables); atomicity preserved in one transaction; pure assertion logic separated from data-copy SQL

issues.description: Relation-parity per-table count subqueries are still written twice (CASE and WHERE) for three relations (moved verbatim, not deduped); a LATERAL would halve it. Carried forward.

Orphaned trigger function work_item_merge_block_tracker_insert survives DROP TABLE tracker_items; the cleanup is only a SQL comment. Make sure the schema-removal task (T19 or later) packet carries the DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS line.
Not matched by tsconfig exclude (src/**/*.test.ts), so it compiles into dist like scratch-schema-test-support.ts. Imports only a type, so harmless.
Counter repair runs on every gated migration, not only while un-migrated rows exist, and takes no row lock. It is monotonic and idempotent, so safe; accepted.

Focus remap matches task_id = old tracker id while remapped sessions keep task_source = 'tracker'. In a hand-built partial state a remapped new card id could equal a still-pending tracker id. Pre-existing T7 design, unreachable in a single-transaction migration.

stage_2.assessment: Important finding cleared: work-item-merge.sql is 277 lines, guard 169, none over 300. Copy DO block is about 235 lines but is now data-copy SQL whose single-transaction atomicity justifies its length; assertions are separated. No behavior change; gating, ordering and crash-loop safety confirmed. Only Minors remain.
